doc.citation: Mehlqvist, K., Wigforss-Lange, J. & Vajda, V. 2015 (for 2014). A palynological study from Sweden reveals stable terrestrial environments during Late Silurian extreme marine conditions. Earth and Environmental Science Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh 105, 149–158.
doc.comment: Twenty newly analysed Klinta samples are extracted individually from Table I. Five additional records reproduce explicit comparison or correlation lists attributed to earlier papers; these are secondary records and require deduplication against those sources. Passing literature mentions without taxon lists are excluded. Klinta has independent Ludfordian marine biostratigraphy; its spores provide a broader Ludlow correlation. Table I combines several morphotaxa and contains spelling inconsistencies, preserved below. For taxa figured in Figure 7, caption names and authorities are retained. Illustrated=true means the taxon is illustrated in this paper; Figure 7 does not identify the source samples. The Klinta section framework derives from Wigforss-Lange (1999, 2007), but this paper presents its first terrestrial palynological investigation.

items.age_basis_detail: Independent Polygnathoides siluricus and Icriodontid conodont zones and Angochitina echinata chitinozoan zone; spores support a Ludlow age.
items.notes: Uppermost sample. Scylaspora klintaensis permits tentative correlation with 112 m in Klinta 1. Section comprises the Bjär and Bjärsjö members; individual sample-to-member assignments are not stated in Table I. Table I prints Dyadospora murusdensa-murusattentata, whereas the prose and diagrams use murusdensa-murusattenuata.

items.age_basis_detail: Age attributed to Mehlqvist et al. (2012); the independent dating evidence for this particular drillcore level is not restated.
items.notes: Secondary occurrence from Mehlqvist, Vajda & Steemans (2012), Early land plant spore assemblages from the Late Silurian of Skåne, Sweden. Only the first appearance of Scylaspora klintaensis at this level is restated. Not a newly analysed sample in this paper; source sample count is not supplied.

items.age_basis_detail: Age of the compared Burgsvik Beds is stated; its dating evidence is not restated.
items.notes: Secondary comparison based on Hagström (1997), Land-derived palynomorphs from the Silurian of Gotland, Sweden, and Gray et al. (1974). Fourteen species are said to be shared with Klinta, but only six are named in that statement. Three additional taxa are explicitly reported from Gotland and absent at Klinta. This is a partial list, not the complete earlier assemblage. No spore percentage data are reproduced. Illustrations in this paper concern Klinta specimens.

items.locality: Rumney Inlier (south Wales) and Towy Anticline (southwest Wales)
items.age_basis_detail: Ludfordian subset selected from the late Wenlock to early Přídolí material of Burgess & Richardson (1995); dating evidence is not restated.
items.notes: Secondary comparison from Burgess & Richardson (1995), Late Wenlock to Early Přídolí cryptospores and miospores from south and southwest Wales, Great Britain. Sixteen taxa are reported for the Ludfordian interval: eleven trilete and five cryptospore taxa. The text gives 69% for trilete dominance; it does not provide individual taxon abundances. Listed shared taxa are not allocated between the two Welsh localities. Laevolancis and Ambitisporites are reported only at genus level. This is a partial list. Illustrations in this paper concern Klinta specimens.

items.formation: McAdam Brook and Moydart formations, Arisaig Group
items.depth_or_level: interval represented by the McAdam Brook and Moydart formations
items.age_basis_detail: The compared interval is described as dated to Ludlow and represented by the libycus–poecilomorphus Assemblage Zone; no independent dating evidence is restated.
items.notes: Secondary comparison from Beck & Strother (2001), Silurian spores and cryptospores from the Arisaig Group, Nova Scotia, Canada. The selected interval contains 25 taxa, but only ten shared species are named here. Deposition is described as more distal, with a larger catchment, than Klinta. Nova Scotia is assigned to western Avalonia explicitly by this paper. A, dilutus retains the printed punctuation. No new specimens from this interval are illustrated.

items.age_basis_detail: Age attributed to Wellman (1993); dating evidence is not restated.
items.notes: Secondary comparison from Wellman (1993), A land plant microfossil assemblage of Mid Silurian age from the Stonehaven Group, Scotland. Formation scope represents a group-level list. Cryptospores constitute c.88% and trilete spores 8% of the assemblage; ornamented triletes are rare. Ten shared species are mentioned, but several are represented only by genus names. This partial list includes three species explicitly present in Scotland but absent at Klinta. Psedodyadospora is the spelling printed in this paper. Illustrations in this paper concern Klinta specimens.
